verdict.rationale: Semgrep documents writing custom rules to control what it detects, plus features that suit secret patterns: an entropy analyzer, generic pattern matching, private org rules and rule testing. Semgrep Secrets itself is documented only for exposed API keys and credentials, with no doc tying custom rules to it. missing for 10: explicit docs for writing custom Semgrep Secrets rules for internal token formats, custom validators for proprietary secrets, independent or hands-on corroboration of custom secret rules.

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can define custom detection rules for my organization's internal token and secret formats

citations.quote: you can write custom rules to determine what Semgrep detects in your repositories
Currently, this syntax supports two analyzers: `redos` and `entropy`.
Users with Semgrep Code's Team or Enterprise tier can publish rules to the Semgrep Registry as private rules that are not visible to those outside their organization.
Semgrep Secrets scans code to detect exposed API keys, passwords, and other credentials.
